step_by_step_reasoning:
1) Inventory: the whiteboard shows AWS (cloud icon), ON-PREM, APACHE METRON, EMR, S3, ATHENA (EMR, S3 and Athena sit inside the Security Data Lake box), SOAR, ALERTS and WAF.
2) Expanding from the audio: the generic AWS cloud icon stands for sources the speaker names explicitly: S3, SNS, SQS, CloudTrail and GuardDuty. I replaced it with 5 separate source nodes. Following ledger rule 4, I attached the AWS->Metron arrow to each of these 5 nodes. The speaker says Apache NiFi builds the pull workflows. I did not add NiFi as a node, because that would send the ledger edge through a new node. NiFi is recorded in the notes instead.
3) Service types: Apache Metron is open-source software. The audio never names an EC2 host for it, so it is ThirdParty. Metron's HDFS backbone is recorded in its notes. SOAR (Blitz, MakeMyTrip's open-source orchestration framework) is ThirdParty. On-prem sources are ThirdParty (syslog/Kafka). ALERTS is a SOC analyst group and an endpoint of ledger edges, so I kept it as UserCompanyAnalyst. WAF maps to WAF.
4) Fusion check: the source-log S3 and the Security Data Lake S3 do different jobs (one is a telemetry source, the other is long-term storage), so they stay as separate nodes.
5) Flows: Flow 0 is hybrid ingestion into Metron, all happening in parallel. Flow 1 is the Security Data Lake: Metron/HDFS -> EMR -> S3 -> Athena, then a feedback loop from Athena back to Metron to build richer profiles over months of data. Flow 2 is incident response: Metron alert -> SOAR enrichment -> analysts -> WAF mitigation.
6) Self-check: there are 9 visual_connections entries. I emit 13 edges, because the AWS->Metron entry became 5 edges after the expansion. 13 >= 9.

graph.name: MakeMyTrip Next-Gen SOC with Apache Metron and Serverless Security Data Lake
graph.categories: Security, SOC, SIEM, Data Lake, Analytics, Incident Response
graph.notes: MakeMyTrip built a next-gen SOC from the ground up. It detects abnormal behavior beyond signature or rule-based detection, for example compromised servers that skew their Producer-Consumer Ratio (PCR). The system covers hybrid ingestion from AWS and on-prem, Apache Metron as the stream-processing core (parsing, enrichment and profiling), a serverless Security Data Lake (EMR -> S3 -> Athena) that feeds profiles back to Metron, and the Blitz SOAR for semi-automated response through WAF, firewalls and routers. Scale: about 20 data sources, about 5,000 events per second, and about 250 million events per day indexed in the data lake. Retention runs to months or years. Next step: threat hunting on the data lake.

nodes.name: S3 (AWS log sources)
nodes.notes: AWS public-cloud telemetry source, expanded from the AWS cloud icon. This is separate from the Security Data Lake S3. Logs are pulled through Apache NiFi.

nodes.name: SNS
nodes.notes: AWS public-cloud telemetry source, expanded from the AWS cloud icon. Integrated through Apache NiFi workflows.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: AWS public-cloud telemetry source, expanded from the AWS cloud icon. Integrated through Apache NiFi workflows.

nodes.name: On-Prem Data Sources
nodes.notes: On-premise telemetry sources. Events are pulled directly into Apache Metron using standard syslog or Kafka integration.

nodes.name: Apache Metron
nodes.notes: The core of the next-gen SOC (stream-processing layer, contributed by Hortonworks). Parsing turns syslog, CloudTrail and GuardDuty logs into a common JSON format. Enrichment adds context such as source IP geolocation, AS number and destination server role (flight, hotel or payment server). Profiling covers only a limited time window, depending on infrastructure. HDFS is the persistence backbone. About 20 sources, about 5,000 events per second.

nodes.name: EMR
nodes.notes: Part of the Security Data Lake. An EMR job picks up persistent data from Metron's HDFS and transforms it into S3. This replaced the earlier on-prem HDFS indexing setup.

nodes.name: S3 (Security Data Lake)
nodes.notes: Serverless, horizontally scalable store for telemetry events, kept for months or years. About 250 million events indexed per day.

nodes.name: Athena
nodes.notes: Runs SQL queries and analytics on S3 data for log mining, analytics and forensics. Generates long-term models and profiles that feed back into Metron. Planned use: threat hunting.

nodes.name: SOAR (Blitz)
nodes.notes: Security orchestration, automation and response framework called Blitz, open-sourced on GitHub. Takes alerts from Metron, adds context such as reverse DNS and WHOIS lookups, and presents everything in a single pane of glass (mobile or Jira integration) to cut triage time.

nodes.name: SOC Analysts (Alerts)
nodes.notes: SOC analysts receive enriched alerts on mobile or Jira and can respond with one click, for example by blocking a source.

nodes.name: WAF
nodes.notes: Mitigation target for semi-automated incident response, for example blocking a source IP. Firewalls and internal routers are also integrated.
